To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cu(II) induced structural transformation of cobalt selenides for remarkable enhancement in oxygen/ hydrogen electrocatalysis.

Cu(II) ion addition to the precursors of CoSe2 nanowires can selectively induce a structural transformation of CoSe2 to Co3Se4, and the resulting Co3Se4/C nanohybrids show remarkably enhanced OER, ORR, and HER catalytic activities.
the synergistic effect between Cu and Co in the Cu 14 Co 3 Se 4 /GC sample is responsible for the high catalytic activities for OER, ORR, and HER.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of multifunctional Cu 14 Co 3 Se 4 /GC catalyst with excellent catalytic activities for OER, ORR, and HER in alkaline media, and the Cu(II) ion induced transformation of the cobalt selenides plays an important role in enhancing the catalytic performance of Co selenides.

the preparation of Cu(II)-induced metastable monoclinine Co3Se4/C hybrid nanorods with remarkable trifunctional activities in alkaline media, which provides a new insight into the design of multifunctional nonprecious catalysts for energy conversion and storage applications.
the design of efficient bifunctional catalysts by using a facile and low-cost strategy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Cu 14 Co 3 Se4/GC hybrid nanomaterials with the synergistic effects of the monoclinic phase of Co 3 Se 4 and the Cu element could serve as a highly efficient multifunctional electrocatalyst for the OER and HER as well as the ORR, which is a promising candidate for electrochemical energy technologies.
Cu 14 Co 3Se 4/GC catalyst exhibits a remarkable trifunctional activity with the highest ORR, OER, and HER activities in the Co-based catalysts.
Cu(II) ion induced structural transformation of cobalt selenides for the remarkable enhancement in electrocatalysis is a promising strategy for designing multifunctional electrocatalysts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cu(II) ion induced structural transformation of Co3Se4 to Cu 14 Co 3 Se 4 could remarkably promote the OER and HER activities.

the Cu 14 Co 3 Se 4/GC catalyst with a high surface area, a large number of exposed active sites, and a high conductivity is a promising multifunctional electrocatalyst for both the ORR and the OER as well as HER.
a trace amount of copper can induce the formation of metastable monoclinine phase Co3Se 4 with enhanced electrochemical activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a synergistic effect between Cu and Co elements is critical to achieve the remarkable electrochemical performances.
Cu(II) induced the transformation of CoSe2 into Co3Se4 and that the synergistic effect between the Cu element, CoSe2 and Co3Se4 played a critical role in the enhanced catalytic activities.
the Cu(II) ion induced structural transformation of the precursors is a facile approach to design efficient multifunctional catalyst for energy storage and conversion technologies.
